entities.summary: Robert Clymer Hendrickson Sr. was an American attorney, Republican Party politician, and diplomat who represented New Jersey in the United States Senate from 1949 to 1955. He also served in local and county offices in Gloucester County, which he represented in the New Jersey Senate from 1934 to 1940, and served as New Jersey Treasurer from 1942 to 1949. After his term as United States Senator expired, President Dwight D. Eisenhower appointed him as United States Ambassador to New Zealand and Samoa from 1955 to 1956.
